classification.difficultyReason: Convert retained-value multipliers to total percentage losses and compare two fleet values.

content.prompt: Taxis depreciate at 50% p.a., and other cars depreciate at 22.5% p.a.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the total percentage depreciation on each type of vehicle after seven years? Give percentages to 2 decimal places.

answer.worked:
The annual retained-value multipliers are $0.50$ and $0.775$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Taxi depreciation}&=(1-0.50^7)\times100\%\\\text{Taxi depreciation}&\approx99.22\%\\\text{Other-car depreciation}&=(1-0.775^7)\times100\%\\\text{Other-car depreciation}&\approx83.21\%\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is the difference in value, to the nearest dollar, after seven years of a fleet of taxis and a fleet of other cars, if both fleets cost $\$1\,000\,000$?

answer.short: $\$160\,111$; the fleet of other cars is worth more.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Taxi fleet value}&=1\,000\,000(0.50)^7\\\text{Other-car fleet value}&=1\,000\,000(0.775)^7\\\text{Difference}&=1\,000\,000(0.775^7-0.50^7)\\\text{Difference}&\approx\$160\,111\end{align*}$$
The fleet of other cars is worth more.
